props.title: World Gone Wild

sections.content: **World Gone Wild** (1987) belongs to the rich tradition of post-apocalyptic films that exploded in the 1980s following the success of Mad Max (1979) and The Road Warrior (1981). This Bruce Dern-starring wasteland adventure combines religious cult dynamics with water scarcity themes, predating similar concerns in Tank Girl (1995) and Waterworld (1995). The film's desert commune setting and battle over resources established tropes that would become standard in the genre, though with a distinctly B-movie charm that sets it apart from bigger budget contemporaries like Steel Dawn (1987).

sections.content: The religious cult elements in **World Gone Wild** (1987) connect it to a specific subset of post-apocalyptic films dealing with fanaticism and organized belief systems, including **Zardoz** (1974) and **Damnation Alley** (1977). The film's villain, a deranged cult leader played by Michael Paré, follows in the tradition of charismatic apocalyptic antagonists like Lord Humungus from The Road Warrior (1981) and later examples like Immortan Joe in **Mad Max: Fury Road** (2015).

The film's environmental messaging about water scarcity was ahead of its time, predating the eco-conscious disaster films of the 1990s. While movies like **A Boy and His Dog** (1975) had touched on resource scarcity, **World Gone Wild** (1987) made it central to its plot, influencing later works like Tank Girl (1995) and Kevin Costner's Waterworld (1995). sections.content: The portrayal of cults in post-apocalyptic cinema took a significant turn with films like **World Gone Wild** (1987). Earlier entries like **Beneath the Planet of the Apes** (1970) featured mutation-worshipping cults, while later films like **Six String Samurai** (1998) and **The Book of Eli** (2010) would continue exploring how belief systems evolve after societal collapse. The film's blend of resource conflict and religious fanaticism created a template that influenced everything from **Hardware** (1990) to **Turbo Kid** (2015).
